name: Giza plateau
summary: Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure on Mokattam limestone, with the chambers and passages already surveyed inside and beneath them.

frame.axes: x east, y north, z up; metres

structures.name: Menkaure
structures.source: Wikipedia, Pyramid of Menkaure (infobox): "29°58′21″N 31°07′42″E", base "102.2 by 104.6 metres", current height "61 m". Base drawn square at the mean side; base elevation from the terrain.

features.name: King's Chamber (Khufu)
features.note: Granite chamber on the pyramid axis, floor about 43 m above the base. Simplified box; placement approximate until re-derived from Petrie (1883).

features.name: Queen's Chamber (Khufu)
features.note: On the pyramid axis, corbelled roof. Simplified box; placement approximate until re-derived from Petrie (1883).

features.name: Grand Gallery (Khufu)
features.note: Corbelled ascending gallery, 46.7 m along its slope. Simplified box; placement approximate until re-derived from Petrie (1883).

features.name: Ascending Passage (Khufu)
features.note: Simplified box; placement approximate until re-derived from Petrie (1883).

features.name: Descending Passage (Khufu)
features.note: Runs from the north entrance down into the bedrock. Simplified box; placement approximate until re-derived from Petrie (1883).

features.name: Subterranean Chamber (Khufu)
features.note: Unfinished, cut into bedrock roughly 30 m below the base platform. Simplified box; placement approximate until re-derived from Petrie (1883).

features.name: ScanPyramids Big Void (Khufu)
features.note: Detected by muon tomography above the Grand Gallery. Length at least 30 m; cross-section and exact position are not tightly constrained. Simplified box; placement approximate until re-derived from Petrie (1883).

features.name: North Face Corridor (Khufu)
features.note: Corridor behind the chevrons on the north face, confirmed by muon imaging and endoscopy. Simplified box; placement approximate until re-derived from Petrie (1883).

features.name: Belzoni's Chamber (Khafre)
features.note: Burial chamber cut partly into bedrock at base level, granite sarcophagus in the floor. Simplified box; placement approximate until re-derived from Petrie (1883).

features.name: Lower Chamber (Khafre)
features.note: Subsidiary chamber on the lower descending passage. Simplified box; placement approximate until re-derived from Petrie (1883).

features.name: Upper Descending Passage (Khafre)
features.note: Simplified box; placement approximate until re-derived from Petrie (1883).

features.name: Lower Descending Passage (Khafre)
features.note: Begins outside the pyramid on the north side and descends into the bedrock. Simplified box; placement approximate until re-derived from Petrie (1883).

landmarks.name: Great Sphinx
landmarks.source: Wikipedia, Great Sphinx of Giza (infobox): "29.97526°N 31.13758°E"; length "73 metres", height "20 metres".

notes: Bedrock: the plateau is Mokattam limestone at or near the surface; its base (-60 m here) and the rock beneath are assumed, not surveyed.
Water table: "The average water table elevation is about +15 m" (Sharafeldin et al. 2019, abstract).

Chambers and passages are simplified boxes from the first investigation; their placement is approximate (the legacy Khufu table ran y southward and is corrected here) and will be re-derived from Petrie (1883) before a Giza simulation relies on them.
Terrain is a DSM: monument footprints are replaced by the surrounding ground and the pyramids are drawn from their survey dimensions.

sources.copernicus: Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, ESA/Airbus, via copernicus-dem-30m.s3.amazonaws.com
